validation.title: Independent aggregate validation of the bounded flow-adaptive pulmonary 0D candidate

protocol.decision_rule: Every required endpoint prediction must lie within one reported cohort standard deviation of the independent mean. Diagnostic endpoints expose limitations but do not determine the qualified validation result.

sources.citation: Forton K, Motoji Y, Deboeck G, Faoro V, Naeije R. Effects of body position on exercise capacity and pulmonary vascular pressure-flow relationships. Journal of Applied Physiology. 2016;121:1145-1150.
sources.license: Publisher terms; only reported aggregate facts are transcribed
sources.measurement_method: Doppler echocardiography in 26 healthy adult volunteers; supine mPAP estimated from tricuspid-regurgitation velocity and cardiac output from the left-ventricular outflow velocity-time integral

sources.citation: Bentley RF, Barker M, Esfandiari S, et al. Normal and Abnormal Relationships of Pulmonary Artery to Wedge Pressure During Exercise. Journal of the American Heart Association. 2020;9:e016339.
sources.license: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0; only reported aggregate facts are transcribed
sources.measurement_method: Right-heart catheterization and triplicate thermodilution cardiac output in 36 healthy controls at semiupright rest and steady-state submaximal exercise

conditions.description: Scope-matched healthy-adult supine rest comparison; the model remains fully locked and receives only the independently reported mean cardiac output.
Independent invasive near-scope crosscheck. Reported mean PAWP is applied as an observed boundary condition; baseline PVR, compliance, and the flow-adaptation rule remain locked.
Independent exercise stress test. Reported mean PAWP and cardiac output are applied as boundary conditions without fitting the Claessen-derived flow-adaptation rule to Bentley.

limitations: Only aggregate means and standard deviations are available; this is not subject-level validation.
Forton et al. used Doppler-derived rather than invasive pulmonary pressure and flow.
Bentley et al. used a semiupright position, whereas part of the declared adaptive range is based on supine exercise.
Applying measured PAWP is boundary conditioning, not parameter fitting; all model parameters remain locked.
Claessen et al. calibrated the flow multipliers and is source- and cohort-disjoint from Bentley et al.; Wright et al. 2016 was explicitly rejected because Bentley reused that Toronto control cohort.
One-standard-deviation compatibility is an engineering acceptance criterion, not proof of statistical equivalence or clinical validity.
